title: School verb paradigm charts (9 pages)
method: Text taken from the PDF font glyphs (glyph names in the embedded David subset, which keep dagesh, shin/sin dots, qibbuṣ and ḥolem-waw that the PDF text layer drops or mis-maps); cells from the drawn table lines; every page checked by eye against a 200-dpi render, with zoomed checks. Cross-check: every transcribed cell compared to the PDF text layer letter-by-letter; all 166 differences are the 5 known text-layer faults (לּ dropped, צּ→ף, קּ→פ, פּ→ע, אֹ ḥolem dropped) plus one qibbuṣ the text layer put in the neighbouring cell.

legend.transcribed: form copied from the school chart
legend.shaded-like-strong: gray cell = the school says this form behaves like the strong verb (no form printed)
legend.footnote-box-area: covered by the school's "** Hifil Wayyiqtol" footnote box
legend.unreadable: not used: no cell was unreadable

idRules: Page 1 uses the strong-verb.json ids (e.g. Qal.yiqtol.2ms/3fs; matchIds lists the strong-verb.json ids it covers). Weak pages prefix the class, e.g. "III-He:Qal.qatal.3ms". "#k" = k-th form in a split cell, counted right-to-left, then top-to-bottom.

notes.text: There is a Qal Yiqtol form that behaves like Peh-Nun, e.g. יִדַּל (from דל''ל).
